entries.reason: After transitionCommunity() in the onboarding community-select handler, reconnectCommunity() is called explicitly: selecting the community that is already active makes transitionCommunity a no-op, and in the browser the onboarding transaction then never advanced past 'Connecting securely…' because nothing else owns the reconnect. onboarding surfaces apply errors and retries connect (finding_4e0ed6b664ebdf19)

attachAgentToChannel short-circuits for a relay-managed harness (isRelayManagedHarness from features/agents/lib/relayManagedHarness): the persona is already a live relay participant, so attaching it is a membership write only (listRelayAgents → addChannelMembers with the persona's pubkey), never a second desktop-managed process. The result's `agent` is therefore typed Pick<ManagedAgent, 'name' | 'pubkey'>. Unknown cloud agent → 'Cloud agent <name> is not registered.' Channel provisioning reuses only agents from agentsReusableUnderPolicy, so reuse never rewrites another instance's access policy (finding_a834349f55c6b2d8). batch member set; relay-managed provision guard (finding_decbe3d324ebf91c)

Pins the roster-trust rule in getMentionableAgentPubkeys: a relay agent listed in `currentChannelAgentPubkeys` is mentionable even when its directory entry has `channelIds: []` and `respondTo: null`, under upstream's required `eligibilityScope`. Upstream's own tests are kept verbatim; our former 'merges relay and persona rows with the same pubkey' case is dropped because upstream's 'coalesces repeated source rows for the same pubkey' test now pins the same behaviour. Tests for roster scoping and restrictive policies (finding_6f268597093fdf72).

Two additive hooks on upstream's eligibility model. (1) `getMentionableAgentPubkeys` takes an optional `currentChannelAgentPubkeys` iterable and adds it to the result unconditionally, alongside upstream's `eligibilityScope`/`phase`: the browser backend's relay-agent directory (`listRelayAgents` in shared/browser-backend/cloudAgents.ts) now answers `respond_to: anyone` and the rooms whose latest 39002 roster lists the persona, but it is a cached directory query refreshed on its own schedule, while the add-member action invalidates the open room's member query at once (useMembersSidebarActions). The channel's signed roster is the membership authority the relay enforces, so a persona added to this room a moment ago is mentionable before the directory refetches; removal is still decided at send time by revalidate_relay_agents against the room's own roster. (2) `coalesceAutocompleteCandidatesByKey` accepts an optional `prefer(candidate, kept)` tie-breaker so a later same-key candidate can replace the kept one in place; mentionCandidates.ts's `preferGlobalSearchIdentity` uses it for kind-0 recency disambiguation. Our former owner-less `pubkey:` identity-key fallback is obsolete: upstream's `agentIdentityKey` now keys agents by pubkey only. The channel roster widens only a channel scope, and a roster agent whose stated policy excludes the viewer is not offered (finding_6f268597093fdf72).
Pins the relay-managed harness set and the model-selectable subset.

isRelayManagedHarness(id) / isRelayManagedModelSelectableHarness(id): the set of harness ids (ferrite-cloud, fabric, a2a) that execute on the relay and need no desktop-managed process. The single source for every relay-managed branch in the agents, onboarding and profile surfaces.

The persona-sync effect returns early when !isTauri(): the web build treats relay kind-0 as the profile authority and has no second local persona store to reconcile, so opening the subscription would only produce DesktopUnavailableError rejections.
adds ferrite-cloud/fabric/a2a to the model-options map so those runtimes are selectable.

Relay-managed harness runtimes (`isRelayManagedHarness` / `isRelayManagedModelSelectableHarness` from features/agents/lib/relayManagedHarness.ts: ferrite-cloud, fabric, a2a) execute on the relay, so the definition dialog must not require a local provider/model pair for them: `runtimeCanChooseLlmProvider` and `customAiPairSatisfied` are short-circuited, `localModeSatisfied` is forced true, the model field is shown only for model-selectable relay harnesses, and picking such a runtime resets the AI configuration mode to defaults and clears provider/model in the selection so Save is never stranded behind a fake 'Custom model' requirement. Separately (security fix, upstreamable), the submitted behavior group goes through `clampBehaviorDraftForOwnerOnly`, so the build's owner-only access lock applies to what is persisted and not only to the disabled access field. Adding or removing environment rows and editing the name pool mark the form changed (finding_21d090a1b937b67e). cleared key removes override; hide only when rendered (finding_c0c17c39e52de0da)

Three fixes to a dropdown that was unusable: the highlight-reset effect keys on a content SIGNATURE instead of array identity (the parent builds filteredOptions inline, so every render snapped the highlight to row 0 and Enter always chose the first model); the search box takes focus inside Radix's onOpenAutoFocus (a render-time ref callback refocused it on every render, and a mount-time ref loses the race with the trigger); and the popover content is pointer-events-auto z-[60] so it stays clickable above a modal dialog that sets pointer-events:none on body. The first two are upstream bugs in upstream's idiom; verify the third against a desktop build before sending.
Pins the signature encoding (a value containing a would-be separator must not imitate two options) and the reset-only-on-content-change behaviour.
The combobox's highlight-reset decision extracted for unit tests: a content-derived signature (JSON tuple encoding, collision-safe) decides when the highlight snaps back to the first row.

`findBuzzCommand` accepts a `buzz` token only in command position (start, after a separator, or behind env/sudo/VAR=value), so `docker run buzz messages send ...` is no longer shown as a sent message, and a flag's value is skipped only when it is not a CLI group, so `buzz --json messages send` is recognised. Error reclassification applies to the generic fallback descriptor too (finding_41121b934fb3fc20). classifyBuzzTool uses the canonical Buzz tool name as its operation, and messages.send counts as a message send (finding_0502d3d4a6c4d9f8).

Pending permission requests are grouped by channel plus JSON-RPC id, each with its own session (the frame's or `params.sessionId`). A response resolves the request from its session, or a sole candidate; an ambiguous response without a session is not stamped on any row. Concurrent sessions, in one channel or across channels, cannot record an outcome on each other's permission rows. The map is bounded. Each session/request_permission in a turn gets its own lifecycle item keyed by its JSON-RPC id (finding_5da62916954356b5); each steer frame gets its own bubble and context, with steered turns tracked for echo suppression (finding_167d1fb82992859b).

Pins per-channel and per-session permission correlation with colliding JSON-RPC ids, the refusal of an ambiguous response, and the bounded pending map. Pairs with the agentSessionTranscript.ts entry. Permission item ids carry the request id; tests for several requests and several steers in one turn (finding_5da62916954356b5, finding_167d1fb82992859b).
A turn display block carries the id of its first item and its key is `turn:<turnId>:<firstItemId>`, so a turn that spans a session boundary no longer produces duplicate React keys and scroll anchors.
Pins unique turn keys across session runs and the new key shape. Pairs with the agentSessionTranscriptGrouping.ts entry.

`extractEventContent` takes an event's content up to the end of its block minus the harness trailer, which is recognised by shape (a `Tags:` line whose value parses as a JSON array, and `Parsed: key=value`, in a contiguous run at the end). A user line starting with `Content:` is not repeated, and user lines starting with `Tags:` or `Time:` are kept even as the final line. Parsing is linear.

Pins that header-like user lines are kept, including a final one right before the trailer, that they are not duplicated, and that only a well-formed trailer is stripped. Pairs with the agentSessionTranscriptHelpers.ts entry.

`applyChannelReset` re-arms paging only when the identity is not known to lack an owner_p subscription, and a new `applyIdentityReset` clears subscription, cursor and hydration, re-arms the one-shot backfill and bumps the generation tokens. Pairs with the useObserverEvents.ts entry.

useLoadArchivedObserverEvents keeps hasOlderArchived false across channel switches for an identity without a subscription, and resets identity-scoped state when the identity changes under a mounted panel, so the new identity's archive is indexed and paged from a null cursor. The backfill and hydration effects key on a probe-settled counter because the reset and probe results can batch into one render. Backfill stops at an identity reset before decrypting or indexing (finding_aef539a267b3bd15) and indexes batch frames by their inner channel via observerFrameChannelId (finding_2752de31dd86bece).

Adds pure tests for the subscription-aware channel reset and the identity reset, and mounted-hook tests for a channel switch without a subscription and an identity change on the same channel. Pairs with the useObserverEvents.ts entry.

huddlesAvailable = isTauri() gates every huddle control: start/join buttons are disabled in a browser tab, their labels and the tooltip say 'Huddles require the Buzz desktop app', and the active-huddle status text says the same. Only the audio-owning window syncs the manual-mute STT gate, including on a relayed mode change (finding_818ae1df005ef3f7).

invokeRawBinary moved into the desktop bridge (there is no window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ to post a raw body to) and the worklet is loaded from ${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}worklet.js, because this bundle is served under /buzz/ui/ and not at the origin root. Also upstreamable (security review F376): a setup that fails after the AudioContext opens (resume, addModule, createMediaStreamSource, new AudioWorkletNode) disconnects whatever nodes it built and closes the context before rethrowing, so retries no longer leak hardware-backed contexts up to the browser's cap. The graph wiring after setup moved into startAudioWorkletTap unchanged. The failure path awaits close() before rethrowing, and the worklet URL falls back to '/' when import.meta.env is absent (the Node test runner) so the module-load failure path is testable.
Pins F376: a failed resume and a worklet that fails to load each close the AudioContext they opened, on every retry.

Security review F149/F150/F377. A KIND_HUDDLE_STARTED is the publisher's own claim (only 48104 is relay-only), so a START from a different author for an existing session no longer replaces it: it leaves the relay-authenticated admissions alone and marks the creator contested, after which only a relay-signed END ends the session (upstream let any member reset a live huddle's roster and inherit END authority with a newer START). A same-author START naming a different parent channel is refused. Session compaction falls back to evicting non-live sessions (nobody present first, oldest start first) when nothing has ended, so the map stays bounded. New HuddleSessionParentRouting decides which parent channel(s) a session's liveness is queried under: relay-signed lifecycle events fix it, a START only adds a capped candidate, and only subscribed channels count. Once a session is contested, no START (including a newer one from its first-seen author) may reset it. Records whether an END was relay-signed; a contested START clears a creator-only END so a backdated START/END pair cannot hide a live huddle (finding_80ac99a47c8ad44b).

Pins F149/F150/F377: a forged START neither resets a live session nor gains END authority (live and history order), a contested session ends only by relay END, parent routing ignores forged STARTs and joins once the relay has spoken, a forged START under the wrong parent does not hide a live huddle in the runtime, and the tracker stays bounded when nothing has ended. Liveness fixtures are relay-signed, and pins that unsigned liveness claiming the relay key keeps no generation (finding_45b3cf9efb0b6a4d). Pins the backdated START/END pair and that a relay END still stands (finding_80ac99a47c8ad44b).

Security review F150: the session-to-parent-channel map used for the authoritative liveness query was last-write-wins over every event's `h` tag, including unauthenticated STARTs, so a forged START could redirect a live session's liveness lookup and hide it. It is now a HuddleSessionParentRouting (huddlePresence.ts) scoped to the viewer's channels, and a session with several candidate parents is queried under each. Every lifecycle event (live and history) must also pass verifyLifecycleEvent (default: id and signature via shared/lib/relayEventSignature) before it reaches the tracker or the routing, because both trust an event's pubkey. Liveness (48104) counts only when signed by the relay's own key and for a requested session (finding_45b3cf9efb0b6a4d).

'retries hydration when one bounded liveness request fails' subscribes to channel-0..channel-128 but its fixtures defaulted to h=general, a channel outside that set that the live subscription could never deliver. The fixtures now carry h=channel-0, because parent routing (F150) only accepts the viewer's channels. The fixtures are unsigned, so every runtime here passes verifyLifecycleEvent: acceptUnsignedFixture; the real signature check is tested in huddlePresenceForgedStart.test.mjs. The liveness fixture is attributed to the relay key, as genuine liveness is (finding_45b3cf9efb0b6a4d).

Security review F375: the resize drag was torn down only by pointerup, so a pointercancel (touch scroll taking over, pen out of range) or a release outside the window left the pointermove listener resizing the column and the body stuck at cursor col-resize / user-select none, stacking listeners on every interrupted drag. pointerup, pointercancel and window blur now all end the drag and detach every listener, a new drag finishes any stale one, and unmount cleans up.
Pins F375: pointercancel, blur and pointerup each restore the body styles and stop resizing; drags never stack; unmount mid-drag cleans up.

canRemoveChannelMember, extracted from MembersSidebar's canRemoveMember so the role rule can be unit-tested. Ours-only because the F145 fix it carries is ours-only until upstream takes it. An owner target (including the viewer's own bot made owner) is offered for removal only to an owner, matching the relay.
Pins F145: an admin is not offered removing an owner; admins and owners keep their other removal rights; self and own-bot removal unchanged.

Security review F145: canRemoveMember let a channel admin remove any other member, owners included, while owners were already barred from removing owners. It now calls canRemoveChannelMember (features/channels/lib/channelMemberRemoval), which refuses an admin acting on an owner. The relay remains the enforcement point. The private-channel add-denied notice shows for a confirmed non-member (membership loaded, viewer absent) instead of never (finding_108de03eddddff99).

Trust rules for the user's own encrypted sidebar blobs (security review F159/F160/F161): isAuthenticOwnSyncEvent checks author, the blob's address (kind and d tag, since every sidebar blob is kind 30078), a plausible created_at and the event id and Schnorr signature before a sync manager lets an event move its watermark or ordering; syncPublishCreatedAt returns a timestamp strictly newer than the known head and at most the local clock plus MAX_SYNC_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS (600 s, inside the relay's 900 s drift window), or null so the publish waits (syncPublishRetryDelayMs) instead of reusing the head's timestamp.

hasValidRelayEventSignature: nostr-tools verifyEvent on a fresh copy of a relay-delivered event. relayClient does not verify signatures, so the sidebar sync managers (F159/F160) and the huddle presence runtime (F149/F150) check here before trusting an event's pubkey.
Test helper: signs sidebar sync fixtures with a real key, because the managers now verify signatures.

Pins F159/F160/F161 for all four sidebar sync managers: a relay-tampered created_at, another author's event and forged live events are refused and never persisted, a wrong-author fetch is 'failed' rather than 'absent', advanceWatermark refuses implausible values and replaces a poisoned one, and a poisoned stored watermark cannot push publishes outside the relay's window.

Security review F161: advanceWatermark persisted any relay-supplied created_at forever, so one forged far-future head stamped every later publish beyond what relays accept and killed the seed path permanently. It now refuses a non-positive, non-integer or implausibly future value and replaces a stored value that is already implausible; readWatermark caps such a legacy value at the skew bound (still > 0, so seed-publish stays blocked). The FetchResult doc now says an unverifiable event is 'failed'.

Security review F160/F161/F396. Fetched and live blobs must pass isAuthenticOwnSyncEvent before they move the watermark, decrypt or decide found/absent; an event that does not verify as the user's own is 'failed', not 'absent' (which pushed a fresh profile into seed-publishing). Publishes are stamped with syncPublishCreatedAt. When another device published after the last head seen, fetchOwnBlobBeforePublish used to return the remote blob and drop the edit that scheduled the publish; it now three-way merges the edit onto the relay's blob against the base the edit was made on (passed by the hook with each publishSections call, kept per queued publish), whenever the relay holds the newest known blob or a newer one, so an edit made before the hook saw this device's own merged publish cannot publish away another device's section (channelSectionsMerge.ts). Publishes that cannot get a strictly newer timestamp wait and retry. getPendingBase and rebasePending let the hook requeue a merged edit against the remote (finding_412874c055f620ab). A publish that finishes while a newer edit is queued moves that edit's merge base to what it published, and the queued publish reads its base when it starts (finding_aec43f6c6769d44d).
The LWW and live-watermark cases feed events signed with a real key (sidebarSyncSignedEvents.mjs), because the manager now verifies signatures (F160). Assertions unchanged.

Per-entry three-way merge of channel sections and assignments (security review F396): local changes against the last synced blob win, everything else comes from the newer remote blob, and assignments to a section neither side kept are dropped. Merged sections are renumbered so equal orders from two devices become distinct (finding_c52b2f753761bd34). reconcileRemoteSections merges pending local edits onto a remote blob (finding_412874c055f620ab).

Pins F396: the record and section merges, and a publish racing a newer remote blob keeping both the local and the remote new section. Regression test for equal section orders from two devices (finding_c52b2f753761bd34). Pins reconcileRemoteSections (finding_412874c055f620ab).

Security review F159/F161: fetched and live mute blobs must pass isAuthenticOwnSyncEvent (author, plausible created_at, id and signature) before they move the watermark or decrypt; a wrong-author event is 'failed', not 'absent'; publishes are stamped with syncPublishCreatedAt. Cancelling a publish drops its pending store, and doPublish settles only the store it carried (finding_dc41d43fc56fe7ec).

Same trust fix as channelMutesSync.ts (security review F160 names all four sidebar managers; F161): verify before trusting pubkey/created_at, wrong author is 'failed', clamped publish timestamp. Cancelling a publish drops its pending store, and doPublish settles only the store it carried (finding_fe7ae1727f4e2ffc).

Same trust fix as channelMutesSync.ts (security review F160 names all four sidebar managers; F161): verify before trusting pubkey/created_at, wrong author is 'failed', clamped publish timestamp. Whole-blob LWW is unchanged here. Cancelling a publish drops its pending store, and doPublish settles only the store it carried (finding_89356d8a9ed0ac2d).
The LWW and live-watermark cases feed events signed with a real key (sidebarSyncSignedEvents.mjs), because the manager now verifies signatures (F160). Assertions unchanged.

Security review F397: applyRemote's setStore updater advanced the applied-remote refs, cancelled the pending publish and wrote localStorage, then guarded on those same refs, so when React ran it twice (StrictMode, restarted concurrent render) the second run returned prev and the merged remote mutes never reached the screen. All of that now happens outside React: a storeRef mirrors the newest store and setStore takes plain values. setMuteState likewise writes and publishes outside the updater. The applied-event refs move only after the merge is stored, and a merge that still carries local changes the remote blob lacks is published instead of cancelling the pending publish. After a reconnect finds the remote blob, the pending store is not republished (finding_97b42046d0b19a3b). Without a relay yet, the pubkey's stored mutes stay loaded instead of resetting to empty (finding_c820f473189c6515).

Security review F400: the same impure-updater fix as useChannelMutes.ts, for stars. Every star read, write and storage listener uses the relay scope, and changes without a relay do nothing (finding_b67bcbc02e282c73).

Security review F398: createSection took its order from a fresh localStorage read while appending to React state, and returned the section even when the write failed (so AppSidebar assigned a channel to a section that did not exist). It now derives the order from the store on screen and returns null when the write fails. setStore resolves updaters once against a storeRef before handing React a value, so the side-effecting updaters here are never replayed. Every mutator passes the store it edited as the publish base (F396), and createSection also refuses a section the store bound did not keep. A remote blob during the debounce window is merged with the unsent local edits and republished when needed, outside React state updaters (finding_412874c055f620ab).

Security review F399: setSortModeFor pruned section sort modes whenever liveSectionIds was truthy, and [] is truthy, so a sort toggle while the sections blob had not loaded (or failed) deleted and published away every per-section preference. Pruning now needs a non-empty list; the store stays bounded by MAX_CHANNEL_SORT_GROUPS. Remote applies and local writes run outside React state updaters through a store ref, and a remote counts as applied only after it is stored (finding_6dd5c5a3eb65d895).

Pins F397/F400 (a remote mute/star beside a pending local change survives StrictMode), F398 (createSection orders from state and returns null on a failed write) and F399 (an empty section list does not wipe section sort modes; a known list still prunes). The stars surface uses the relay-scoped storage key (finding_b67bcbc02e282c73).
Pins the archiveAvailable gate on the two startup archive hooks: without a local archive neither merges, warns, nor reports observer readiness; deps without the flag keep upstream's behaviour.

AgentMetricArchiveSeedDeps gains an optional archiveAvailable (default isTauri) and the effect returns before seeding when it is false. The browser seam refuses merge_save_subscription_kinds (there is no SQLite archive), and because a failed seed persists no marker the hook retried and logged a DesktopUnavailableError on every AppShell mount. Injected deps without the flag behave exactly as upstream.

ObserverArchiveSeedDeps gains an optional archiveAvailable (default isTauri); startReconciliation returns a no-op cancel without attempting reconciliation or calling onReady when it is false, so the browser build never starts archive sync and never logs the refused merge on each mount. Injected deps without the flag behave exactly as upstream.

The local archive writes a SQLite database in the Buzz nest, which a browser tab cannot do. archiveAvailable = isTauri() is threaded as an `available` prop into ObserverArchiveSection and AgentMetricArchiveSection (their switches are disabled when false), disables the add-subscription and remove-subscription buttons, and renders a role=alert notice (local-archive-browser-unavailable) that relay history remains available in the browser. Upstream's removal of the observer policy gate is taken as-is. gate on native archive commands (finding_1c0b6bbaae37e8a1)

The MCP connector settings surface: catalog API client for the relay's /buzz/api/mcp/* routes, pure row-state logic with its tests (connected / not granted / unavailable kept apart), and the settings card with the authenticate button. Upstream has no equivalent surface — their MCP servers are configured per local harness.

useDeleteMessageMutation.onSuccess removes the row through applyLocalMessageDeletion (lib/localMessageCacheUpdates.ts: window store, flattened timeline and the channel's thread-reply caches) instead of filtering the flattened timeline alone, which the next live event re-projected from the window store, so the deleted row reappeared (F378). useSendMessageMutation.onError removes only the failed optimistic row via rollbackOptimisticSend instead of restoring the pre-send snapshots, which dropped every live event that arrived during the send and was a no-op when no window existed, leaving a ghost 'sending' row (F379); the mutation context therefore carries only optimisticId and channelId. Same defects upstream; send them. The send mutation records and clears the timeout only in the scope it started in (finding_2d613e60ee3ff2a0). Edit and delete mutations pin the channel they were started in; an edit rewrites earlier edit overlays and the thread caches (finding_87f712150a349d5f); a window fetch reconciles against the messages cached after it, not before (finding_254e812b75656f85).

Pins the JSON-snapshot rule above (a .agent.json/application/json clipboard item restores the attachment) and that a .agent.json name with a PNG type is refused. Upstream's assertions are unchanged. Also pins that a pasted snapshot whose name or filename carries line breaks, control characters or a bidi override is refused (F151). Primes the relay origin for the fixtures and pins that a snapshot URL on another host is refused (finding_83f3010cb4b8e8a3).

parseAgentSnapshotClipboardHtml also accepts JSON snapshots: a filename matching /\.(agent|team)\.json$/ with type application/json is restored as an attachment (type application/json), beside upstream's PNG rule; the team size limit keys on '.team.' in the name rather than the .team.png suffix. Hosted agents here are exported as .agent.json definitions (the relay's agent catalog), not only as PNG-embedded cards. Also refuses a displayName or filename containing a line break, another control character or a bidirectional override (security finding F151): the name is written into the outgoing Markdown attachment link, so a crafted clipboard could otherwise end the link and append its own paragraphs to a message the victim signs. That part is the same defect upstream; send it to them. A pasted snapshot URL must be on the cached relay origin, under /media/ or /blob/, with no userinfo; any other host would be fetched as soon as the paste renders (finding_83f3010cb4b8e8a3).
Pins that a started upload reaches exactly one onSettled: after a forced silent reset, after an ordinary cancel (following onCancel), and after an empty upload completes (F380).

start()/enqueue take an optional onSettled callback, invoked exactly once when the task reaches any terminal state, including cancelTask with notify: false (resetBackgroundMediaUploads), which suppresses onCancel while the task loop skips onComplete and onError. A sender awaiting the upload settled only from those three and hung forever (F380). Same defect upstream; send it.
Pins that same-named global-search identities with different pubkeys both stay candidates, whichever arrives first and whatever their kind-0 timestamps (F152/F158).

Upstream moved candidate construction here from useMentions.ts; this build's relay-as-only-profile-store intent moves with it. (1) profileCreatedAt is carried on every candidate: addCandidate merges it with Math.max when a member row and a global-search hit for the same pubkey collapse (only the search side carries the kind-0 timestamp), member rows get profileRecency(profile), search rows get user.createdAt; useMentions orders by it. (2) Same-named global-search identities are NOT coalesced (upstream coalesces them by display name and nip05 label): every input to that collapse is chosen by the identity's owner, so it let an impostor hide the genuine person and take the mention's p tag (security findings F152/F158). Each pubkey keeps its own row. (3) Persona candidates come from personaMentionCandidates(activePersonas, managedAgentPersonaIds, relayAgents, isArchived) (additive), which resolves cloud teammates to the pubkey that makes their mention a p tag instead of a local-harness provisioning request a browser cannot fulfil. Everything else is upstream's.

Pins one render key per sent row: an acknowledged event's localKey survives a head refetch (replaceNewestChannelWindow), a second refetch, and an acknowledgement that arrives after the page already holds the row; rows not sent from this tab are untouched.
Two-page round-trip test for the bounds-key derivation above.

The channel-window bounds key must be derived from the REQUEST cursor, because in this build the window comes from the relay's /window route via the browser backend rather than a local Rust cache, and page two silently mismatched the head-page key. Paired with the additive shared/api/channelWindowKey.ts.

carryLocalKeys: replaceNewestChannelWindow copies an acknowledged event's localKey (from the retained overlay or pages) onto the matching relay page row, and mergeLiveChannelWindowEvent adopts a late acknowledgement's localKey onto a row the page already holds. Relay pages carry no localKey, so every head refetch (reconnect, auto-heal invalidation) moved a sent row's render key from optimistic-<uuid> to the relay id and remounted it. Same defect upstream; send it to them. Also adds removeChannelWindowEvents(store, ids), the removal counterpart of mapChannelWindowEvents, used by lib/localMessageCacheUpdates.ts so a local delete or a failed-send rollback edits the store rather than only the flattened cache (F378/F379).

Two fixes. (1) The schema's parseHTML no longer trusts pasted HTML: a span whose data-href does not resolve through resolveComposerMessageLinkAttributes is not a chip, the href is canonicalised and the channel name comes from the local channel list, and renderText/markdown serialize write only a canonical href (canonicalComposerMessageLinkHref). A crafted clipboard could otherwise publish arbitrary text under the victim's key behind an innocuous 'Buzz link' chip (F153). (2) The markdown-it rule resumes a split `buzz` + `://…` link only when that `buzz` starts a word, so `notbuzz://…` stays prose (F381). Same defects upstream; send them.

Mounts the production composer and pastes attacker HTML: an unresolvable chip href and a crafted or unknown emoji shortcode never become nodes or reach the Markdown, a resolvable chip is canonicalised and named locally, a known emoji's image comes from the palette, and a custom-emoji node restored from JSON never renders its own src; plus a spoilered URL never reaching the link-preview input and markdown restore keeping `notbuzz://…` as prose (F153, F154, F156, F381).

parseHTML accepts a pasted only when its shortcode is well-formed ([a-z0-9_-]) and in the community palette, never takes the pasted src, and renderHTML takes the image URL only from the palette (a node restored from JSON with an unknown shortcode renders no URL rather than its stored src), and renderText/markdown serialize write nothing for a malformed shortcode. A crafted clipboard could otherwise make the composer fetch an image from any origin on paste and smuggle text into the sent message through data-shortcode (F154). Same defect upstream; send it.

The deletion tests now sign the deletion with the target's author (they modelled an author's delete with a stranger's key), plus tests that a stranger's kind:5/9005 hides neither a message nor a reaction, that an unheld target hides nothing, and that only relay-signed kind:40099 rows render (F155/F157).

Two authorship rules the renderer lacked. (1) collectAuthorizedDeletionTargets: a kind:5/9005 hides its target only when the target is held and the deletion's signer also signed it, the rule the relay applies before erasing (effects::apply_deletion); the relay stores and delivers a stranger's deletion, so honouring every marker let any room member blank anybody's message for every reader (F155). Used by formatTimelineMessages, countTopLevelTimelineRows and collectReactionActorPubkeys. (2) isRelaySignedSystemMessage: a kind:40099 system row renders only when signed by the active relay (NIP-11 self), since any member can submit that kind and forge membership history or moderator removals (F157); countTopLevelTimelineRows takes the relay identity as an optional second argument. Same defects upstream; send them. Two edits in the same second resolve by the larger event id whatever their arrival order (finding_b88ceeaf3949e40f).
Pins that line breaks in an attachment label or filename stay inside the one Markdown link line (F151).

formatImetaMediaLine collapses line breaks and other control characters in the attachment label to a space before escaping it: the label sits inside one Markdown link on one line, and a newline from a pasted snapshot name or crafted filename published the rest as the sender's own paragraphs (F151). Bidi embedding, override and isolate controls (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069) collapse the same way, so a filename cannot display as a different name. Same defect upstream; send it.

buildPreviewUpdate blanks the characters of spoiler-marked text runs (same length, so offsets hold) in linkPreviewContent. The plain-text projection carries no marks, so the ||…|| delimiters the preview extractor masks spoilers by were gone and a URL typed inside a spoiler was resolved, previewed and published in the event's link-preview tags (F156). Same defect upstream; send it. Blanks code blocks (keeping line breaks) and code-marked runs in the preview input, as spoilers are, so a URL inside code is never fetched or published in link-preview tags (finding_6dc1dd9f12fb2c26).

Real QueryClient and projection: a deleted row stays gone after the next live event and leaves open thread caches, a failed send removes only its optimistic row and keeps concurrent live events, and a failed send with no prior window leaves no ghost row (F378/F379).

applyLocalMessageDeletion and rollbackOptimisticSend, used by hooks.ts: remove events from the window store (removeChannelWindowEvents), the flattened timeline and the channel's thread-reply caches, then re-project, so a local delete or failed-send rollback is not undone by the next live merge (F378/F379).
Pins that parseSystemMessagePayload keeps only well-typed fields (F157).

parseSystemMessagePayload validates the parsed body field by field instead of casting it: a JSON object with a string type, string-only actor/target/topic/purpose/public_reason/reason_code/action_id, and filtered targets/arrivals, so a crafted non-string never reaches normalizePubkey or the renderer (F157). Same defect upstream; send it.

Pins the recency ordering above, including the clamp of a future-dated profile and that 60 fresh same-named outsider impostors cannot push an older genuine outsider past the 50-row cap (F158). The tie-break tests for the removed same-name collapse are gone.

Same-named identities are never collapsed onto one suggestion (security findings F152/F158): upstream's globalSearchIdentityKey collapse, and the kind-0-recency tie-break this build once added to it, decided the survivor from values the identity's owner chooses (display name, nip05 label, created_at), so an impostor could remove the genuine person from the picker and receive the mention's p tag. globalSearchIdentityKey and preferGlobalSearchIdentity are removed; every pubkey keeps its own row and MentionAutocomplete's collision npub disambiguates. orderMentionCandidatesByRecency stays for channel members (the relay is this build's only profile store and accumulates same-named roster profiles, so the live colleague must sort first) and clamps a future-dated created_at to now; an outsider found only by global search gets no recency, since anyone can mint same-named profiles with fresh timestamps and push an older genuine outsider past the 50-row cap, so outsiders keep the search's own order. Upstream has the destructive collapse too; send the removal to them.
Pins pubkey resolution, archived-agent exclusion, and dedup against identities already in the candidate list. Tests for archived namesakes and pubkey normalisation (finding_bf9929a8a34b8de3).

Resolves a relay-backed persona mention candidate to an identity carrying that agent's PUBKEY (archived agents excluded), so the mention becomes a p tag. Without it the composer tries to provision a local harness runtime for the persona — which a browser cannot do — and the send fails with no dialog and no relay write. Agents are grouped by name and the first one that is bound, live and admits the viewer wins, with normalised pubkeys (finding_bf9929a8a34b8de3).
The regression test that pins the timeline-latch fix. Goes upstream with the fix.
Same defect class as MessageTimeline: the snapshot path had to stop discarding the live tail once the latch was fixed. Goes upstream with it.
Pins composerMayTakeFocus: nothing focused or a plain button takes focus; a text-entry surface or anything inside an open popover, menu, dialog or alertdialog keeps it.

composerMayTakeFocus adds one guard to upstream's: autofocus does not take focus from an element inside an open overlay ([data-radix-popper-content-wrapper], dialog, alertdialog, menu). The effect re-fires when the editor's focus callback changes identity (measured on a relay reconnect), and taking focus from a menu item made Radix dismiss the overlay as focus-outside, so the profile popover closed under the pointer. Same defect upstream; send it to them.

Two hooks on upstream's refactored composer flow. (1) `currentChannelAgentPubkeys` — members of the current channel flagged as agents (`member.isAgent`, `role === 'bot'`, or present in the managed/relay agent name maps) — is memoised and passed to `getMentionableAgentPubkeys` next to upstream's `eligibilityScope`/`phase: 'prepare'`, because this build's relay directory carries no channel ids or respond-to policy and would otherwise hide every cloud agent that is already a room member. (2) `rankMentionCandidates` is fed `orderMentionCandidatesByRecency(mentionCandidatesWithTeams)` so the kind-0-newest identity survives the 50-row slice on a relay holding many same-named profiles. Candidate construction (profileCreatedAt propagation, `profileRecency`, `personaMentionCandidates`) no longer lives in this file: upstream moved it to features/messages/lib/buildMentionCandidates.ts, which needs its own entry carrying that intent. A null flush cancels a deleted inline mention and gives the key back, or selects a bare @ at its fresh offset (finding_b5b336be71ce4010).

Beyond upstream's one-shot hydration, subscribes to live reactions for exactly the rendered message ids via relayClient.subscribeToMessageReactionsLive (ours-only in shared/api/relayClientSession.ts, filter from buildVisibleReactionLiveFilter in shared/api/relayChannelFilters.ts) and merges each event into channelMessagesKey(channelId) with mergeMessages; disposal is guarded so a late subscription resolve is torn down. The dependency is the joined id list, not the entry arrays. Needed because the relay is the only reaction store here and the browser's polled HTTP transport has no channel-wide live feed to piggyback on.

The TipTap Link extension is configured with `protocols: []` plus `isAllowedUri: (url, { defaultValidate }) => parseMessageLink(url).ok || defaultValidate(url)` instead of `protocols: ['buzz']`. Registering `buzz` re-registers the scheme with the linkifyjs singleton on every composer mount after the first, which logs a warning and makes scheme state depend on mount order; the sanitiser only needs to admit a structurally valid message deep-link (`parseMessageLink` from ./messageLink). Upstream's `linkOnPaste: false` is kept. Same defect upstream; send it to them and delete this entry. The DOM paste guard uses composerLinkPasteYields (finding_e417483e4398a331).

virtua's itemSize option is a number, not a per-item callback; upstream passes an estimator FUNCTION, which virtua 0.49.3 destructures as a plain value — arithmetic on a function object for every unmeasured row. Replaced with UNMEASURED_TIMELINE_ROW_HEIGHT = 60, the estimator's own documented floor. Both a type error and a runtime defect; goes upstream with TimelineMessageList.tsx.

hasReplyAction also gates on !message.pending. Replying to a not-yet-confirmed row hands its client-minted optimistic-<uuid> id to the send path, which publishes an e tag naming an id that can never exist on any relay — a DURABLE reference every client then renders as a reply to nothing, and a thread panel opened on it skeletons forever once the confirmed row swaps to its real id. The adjacent hasCopyActions and canReport already gate on pending for the same class of reason, so this is one line in upstream idiom; the desktop has the same race with a narrower window, hence upstreamable rather than browser-only.

A Virtua at-bottom flap is swallowed by a one-way suppression latch, so after the viewer's OWN first send the rendered tail freezes permanently and every later live event lands in the query cache unrendered. Reproduced live in two clients; this is a bug in UPSTREAM's product, not a browser adaptation — send it to them and delete this entry.

Passes the constant unmeasured-row height into the virtualizer instead of upstream's estimator function (virtua itemSize expects a number — see virtualizedTimelineItems.ts). Bites specifically in the virtualized path where useContentVisibility={false} switches off the per-item CSS reservation.
A relay edit refusal (finishEdit throwing, with or without a deferred attachment upload) restores the draft and surfaces the error message via setUploadError instead of silently dropping the edit.
Pins that a relay edit refusal restores the draft and reports the failure message both with and without a deferred upload. Pairs with the submitMessageEdit.ts entry.
Upstream's helper tests verbatim plus one case pinning isDesktopUnavailableError: recognised by error name, not by message text, and a plain string is not an error.

Exports isDesktopUnavailableError(error): true only for an Error whose name is 'DesktopUnavailableError', which is what the browser desktop-bridge throws for a command only the shell answers. useMentionSendFlow.ts uses it to skip huddle enrollment in a tab without masking any other failure. Pinned by useMentionSendFlow.helpers.test.mjs. draftAgentPredicate (finding_c9bc0036379e83e7).

Two browser adaptations on upstream's send flow. (1) `invokeTauri('sync_agents_to_active_huddle')` failing with a `DesktopUnavailableError` (recognised via `isDesktopUnavailableError` from useMentionSendFlow.helpers.ts; the browser desktop-bridge throws it for desktop-only commands) is logged and skipped so a text mention still publishes; any other huddle-enrollment error stays blocking exactly as upstream. (2) In `createMentionedPersonaAgents`, a created agent is pushed to `agents` (later `preparedManagedAgents`, fed to the process-start readiness pass) only when it has a `status` field: hosted cloud agents are relay participants without a local ManagedAgent process and are ready after the membership write. Our former lazy `getManagedAgentsByPubkey` call and the finishSend failure toast are obsolete: upstream now catches the directory fetch and toasts via `formatMessageSendError`. Adds `subscribeToMessageReactionsLive(messageIds, onEvent)` using the ours-only `buildVisibleReactionLiveFilter` in shared/api/relayChannelFilters.ts for render-scoped NIP-25 reaction delivery on both transports (consumer: features/messages/lib/useRenderScopedReactionHydration.ts). The ensureConnected-before-publish ordering is the upstreamable part; the HTTP transport is browser-only in nature and could move to an additive shared/api/relayHttpTransport.ts to shrink this file's divergence. Publish ownership is captured before initial connection and checked after connection and before HTTP digest/sign/fetch admission; community-switch cancellation cannot fall through to HTTP or sign with a replacement identity. Ordinary same-owner outages preserve the identical signed event retry. Reads and live subscriptions cancelled by a disconnect rethrow instead of falling back to HTTP in the next session (finding_d9093a2660a7beb3); gated reads pass a session check (finding_0a06a7863fa0712b).
